title: Continuous batcher: length-drift mitigation and GPU memory slimming
creator: Marcus Holt
description:
Background: Production traffic shows multi-modal prompt/response length distributions: short instruction-only requests, medium multi-turn chats, and long-document summarizations. Continuous batcher currently uses fixed slotting heuristics and hard KV reservation thresholds which cause two problematic behaviors when workload 'length drift' occurs (a) transient KV over-reservation leading to GPU slab fragmentation and higher OOM + cold evictions, and (b) longer tail latency for medium/long responses due to conservative coalescing that prevents efficient packing of short requests into leftover slots.

Goal: Reduce 99th-percentile tail latency regressions during mixed-length drift while lowering per-token GPU memory footprint and token-cost by improving slot utilization and KV residency without increasing average latency. Target metrics: 99th latency <= baseline+10ms, 50-90th latency equal or improved, KV eviction events down >=30%, per-token GPU memory usage down >=6%, production cost/unit down >=5% after rollout.

Proposed approach: "Length-drift mitigation and GPU slimming" is a 3-part approach:
1) Adaptive Horizon Windowing: maintain a short rolling distribution of recent sequence-lengths per cohort (user, route, model) and compute a sliding 'preferred slot size' with exponential decay. Use this to bias the batcher to assemble batches that minimize wasted padding without creating long-lived KV reservations.
2) Soft-KV Compression (runtime): introduce an optional in-memory compact representation for cold KV entries where rarely-accessed KV shards are stored compressed and can be decompressed on demand. Compression uses a fast LZ4-like path with budgeted decompression latency; compressed KV entries reduce slab footprint for long contexts.
3) Slot Slimming + Aggressive Packing: implement a slot slimming policy that allows short-lived overpacking of short sequences into leftover token-capacity within a slot with a strict latency budget guardrail. When the guardrail is hit, the batcher falls back to conservative packing. This is implemented as a token-budget-aware admission controller in the scheduler.

Design details:
- Cohort definitions: by route+model+client-region. Rolling window = 2000 requests or 60s, whichever is first. Exponential decay factor alpha=0.12.
- Preferred slot size computed as weighted 75th percentile of recent sequence lengths per cohort (tunable).
- Soft-KV compression triggered when cohort KV residency exceeds threshold R_high (default 72% slab occupancy). Decompression budgeted to <2ms average per decompression path to avoid tail spikes.
- Slot slimming admission: allow packing up to 15% extra tokens in a slot if expected added latency <= 6ms based on microbench predictor.
- Fallback policy: if 99th latency deviation > target for the last 5 minutes, revert to current stable slotting and disable soft-KV compression for that cohort.

Experimentation plan:
- Stage 0 (bench): run simulators with replayed traffic from last 30 days (sanitized) across three representative clusters (short-skew, mixed, long-skew). Measure KV evictions, slab fragmentation, average and tail latencies, decompression CPU/GPU impact.
- Stage 1 (canary): rollout to 2% of traffic for two low-risk customer cohorts. Monitor: 99/95/50 latency, KV evictions, GPU memory headroom, CPU decompression load.
- Stage 2 (ramp): 10% -> 25% -> 50% with automated rollback triggers (latency deviations, error rate, OOMs).
- Stage 3 (full): enable runtime for all cohorts with moderate throttling to avoid simultaneous mass decompressions.

Metrics and observability:
- Instrument new metrics: cohort_preferred_slot_size, cohort_kv_residency_ratio, slot_slimmed_count, soft_kv_decompressions_total, soft_kv_decompression_latency_p50/p95, batcher_revert_events.
- Dashboards: per-route cohort dashboard and aggregate runtime-1.22 rollout dashboard. Add alerts for >3x baseline soft_kv_decompression rates or any increase in GPU OOMs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bench: simulated cost per token down >=6% on mixed and short-skew traces without >5% increase in average latency.
- Canary: 2% traffic shows no more than +10ms 99th latency and >=20% reduction in eviction events.
- Ramp: at 50% traffic cumulative per-token cost improvement sustained and no regression in error rates or OOMs.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: decompression increases CPU utilization causing host-level contention. Mitigation: cap decompression concurrency and offload to dedictated CPU pool; add early disable flag.
- Risk: adaptive horizon oscillation on ephemeral surges. Mitigation: exponential decay + hysteresis and minimum stabilization window of 10s.
- Risk: slower cold-path when compressed KV decompresses during hot-turn. Mitigation: prefetch heuristics for likely-to-be-accessed KV shards and local hot-reservation for last-N active sessions.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- Scheduler: add cohort tracker and preferred slot calculation (ENG changes + unit tests).
- Runtime: implement compressed KV store with fast path and metrics.
- Admission: token-budget-aware admission controller and latency predictor integration.
- Observability: new metrics and dashboard, add canary automation with rollback triggers.

Acceptance artifacts: benchmark results (links in comments), PRs for scheduler/runtime, updated runbook for rollback, and canary dashboard template.

Notes: This ticket focuses on scheduler and runtime engineering; separate follow-ups will add model-variant routing and quantization synergy (future work).
